identity: An Arabic online tech-news report (news-wire register, c. 10 April 2013) about the German hacker and former pilot Hugo Teso, who demonstrated an Android app (PlaneSploit) able to break into aircraft control systems. PASS 1 / granularity (doctrine 0e): it is a headline line plus six body paragraphs delimited by <NL>. There is no list, no table, no MCQ stem+option pattern, no verse, no isnad, no legal article, no workbook drill, and no dialogue. So the genre declares no unit of its own and the default applies: genre A/G factual-journalistic prose, whose native unit is the clause-sized information chunk. The headline (tokens 0-11) is a printed line and therefore exactly one unit.
law: PASS 2 / connectives. Default at every wa and every fa is CUT; I must actively justify a merge, never the reverse. A conjunct MERGES only when (a) it is a bare noun, adjective or participle hanging off the same governor (al-wilayat al-muttahida al-amrikiyya wa-Uruba; al-bramijiyyat wa-l-'atad; ish'al wa-itfa' sharing one object; tasmim ... wa-nashriha sharing one predicate), or (b) it COMMENTS on the proposition just stated rather than advancing past it (anaphoric wa-dhalika athna'a...). A conjunct CUTS when it brings a new predicate PLUS material of its own: a finite verb with its own object or frame, or a coordinated verbal noun with its own complement (doctrine G2/F1). Never cut after the tight subordinators li-anna, kay, bi-haythu, hatta, illa athna'a, or after alladhi/allati-marked relatives; never split a fa-idha protasis from its apodosis. Always cut before lakin/wa-lakin, idh, fa-idha, a clause-initial fa, and a speech verb opening a new report (qala, a'lana, ashara, adafa, istatrada) - and inside reported speech the same laws keep running (A11). The one syntactic call this document turns on: an ASYNDETIC post-nominal clause that carries its own predication opens a unit (A6), whereas a relative marked by alladhi/allati never does.
reasoning: Sites I had to argue. (1) @38 'andrud' -> 'yasmah bi-ikhtiraq...': yasmah is an unmarked clausal modifier of the indefinite object tatbiqan, stranded five tokens from its head behind an intervening allati-relative. Doctrine A6 (`...ala a'da' kahrabaiyya || tatakawwan min khalaya khassa...`) is the direct precedent: an asyndetic descriptive continuation on an indefinite noun CUTS in this genre. Against it: the connective table says alladhi/allati never opens a unit, and this modifier completes the object NP. Deciding factor: without the cut, unit 1 runs 43 tokens, which is not clause-sized in a corpus that segments into information chunks. CUT, lo. (2) @45 'bi-l-ta'ira' -> 'wa-i'ta'iha awamir tughayyir... aw tursil...': a two-item masdar coordination under one yasmah bi-. F8 shows a conjunct sharing a governor merging (wa-mughallafan bi-l-lawn al-akhdar), but there the conjunct had only a PP; here it carries its own object plus two finite relative clauses, which is the F1/G2 shape (wa-nahran yajri abra sad', wa-sayriha ala aqdam ghariba). Weight beats syntax. 0d does not cancel it: it advances a second distinct capability, it does not evaluate the first. CUT, lo. (3) @128/@132/@135 in P2: wa-istata'a governs a four-item enumeration of verbal nouns - al-tahakkum bi-ajhizat al-takyif li-taghyir..., wa-ish'al wa-itfa' al-anwar al-janibiyya, wa-l-ta'arruf ala mawqi'iha, wa-taghyir masariha. G2 cut a comparable masdar enumeration and even let a one-word muraqabatiha end a unit; B2 says parallelism defeats the short-tail brake, so the 2-token wa-taghyir masariha still cuts. Inside item 2, wa-ish'al is a bare masdar sharing al-anwar with wa-itfa', so no cut there - the same wa, opposite verdicts, exactly the F8 miniature. (4) @137 NOT cut: wa-dhalika athna'a tashghil al-ta'ira is an anaphoric journalistic coda pointing back at what was just narrated - the wa-hadha ma fa'alat-hu al-tifla shape that gold absorbed (@951). I was inclined to cut it for its temporal frame; 0d cancels the cut, which is the only legal use of 0d (§3.5).
